extracted.intended_audience: USDA program staff, lenders, borrowers, and legal/regulatory practitioners working with the OneRD Guaranteed Loan Program (7 CFR Part 5001)
extracted.subtask_description: Clarifications and technical corrections to the OneRD Guaranteed Loan Regulation (7 CFR part 5001), including definitions (affiliate, commercially available), eligibility rules for Business & Industry projects, limits on agricultural production financing, exceptions, and REAP renewable energy system eligibility requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliate (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Affiliate means a person or entity that is closely attached or connected to another person or entity. For the purposes of program eligibility, the principles outlined in 13 CFR 121.301(f), and any successor regulation, are used to establish affiliation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the revised §5001.3 definition of 'Affiliate' adopted to clarify affiliation for program eligibility determinations under the OneRD guaranteed loan regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercially available (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercially available means a system that meets the requirements of either paragraph (1) or (2) of this definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph (1) — A domestic or foreign system that: (i) Has both a proven and reliable operating history and proven performance data for at least one year specific to the use and operation to the proposed application; (ii) Is based on established design and installation procedures and practices and is replicable; (iii) Has professional service providers, trades, large construction equipment providers, and labor who are familiar with installation procedures and practices; (iv) Has proprietary and balance of system equipment and spare parts that are readily available; (v) Has service that is readily available to properly maintain and operate the system; and (vi) Has an existing established warranty that is valid in the United States for major parts and labor. Paragraph (2) — A domestic or foreign system that has been certified by a recognized industry organization whose certification standards are acceptable to the Agency. This is the added/clarified §5001.3 definition of 'Commercially available.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Agricultural production eligibility for B&I projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Agricultural production is eligible as part of Business & Industry (B&I) guaranteed loan financing only when it is not eligible for Farm Service Agency (FSA) farm loan programs assistance and when it is part of an integrated business also involved in the processing of agricultural products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any agricultural production considered for guaranteed loan financing must be owned, operated, and maintained by the business receiving the guaranteed loan. Examples of potentially eligible agricultural production include but are not limited to an apple orchard in conjunction with a food processing plant; poultry buildings linked to a meat processing operation; or sugar beet production coupled with storage and processing. (This text revises §5001.105(b)(7).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on agricultural production portion of any loan
rubrics_metrics.description: The agricultural production portion of any loan must not exceed 50 percent of the total loan or $5 million, whichever is less.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the quantitative cap applied to agricultural production financing within a B&I guaranteed loan (see §5001.105(b)(7)(i)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to agricultural production portion limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: The 50 percent/$5 million limitation does not apply to certain types of businesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed exceptions (per §5001.105(b)(7)(ii)): (A) Commercial nurseries engaged in production of ornamental plants, trees, and other nursery products (bulbs, flowers, shrubbery, seeds, sod, growing plants from seed to transplant stage); (B) Forestry (operation of timber tracts, tree farms, forest nurseries, harvesting forest products, reforestation); (C) Growing or harvesting of mushrooms; (D) Growing of hydroponics; (E) Boarding and/or training of animals; (F) Commercial fishing; and (G) Production of algae and aquaculture, including conservation, development, and utilization of water for aquaculture.

rubrics_metrics.name: REAP Renewable Energy System (RES) project eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: For a REAP RES project to be eligible for a loan guarantee under this part, it must meet the criteria specified in §5001.102(a) through (c) and in paragraphs (a) through (e) of §5001.106 and be for a borrower eligible to submit an application for the project in accordance with §5001.126.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If taxable bonds are utilized as debt instruments the provisions of §5001.105(b)(19) must also be met. (This revises the introductory paragraph of §5001.106.)
